correctness.rationale: Kaib–Werner Lemma 5.11 gives divisibility and Proposition 6.12(2) finite flat surjective multiplication for every m≠0. The constant finite-flat kernel length is m^(2g-t_eta); the identity special-fiber length is m^(2g-t_s). Over algebraically closed residue fields, divisibility on the identity component moves each m-torsion component representative into N_s[m], and translation shows every occupied component has exactly the connected kernel length. Their ratio proves the exact formula even when residue characteristic divides m; divisibility then identifies each Prüfer rank. Neither the torsion-free divisible summand nor nonclosed-F cases are determined.
residual_risks: The rank computation relies on the claimed semi-abelian fiberwise identity structure and the exact source theorem; no independent reproving of the deep existence theorem is attempted.

value.rationale: The Prüfer rank identifies exactly how far torus rank rises in every fiber of an arbitrary-rank valuation spectrum, turning a qualitative component-divisibility result into a quantitative intrinsic structural law useful for reduction-theoretic comparisons. It handles all m scheme-theoretically rather than just point-count heuristics, although the deduction after the source inputs is short.
residual_risks: No information about a torsion-free Q-vector-space component of Phi_s; closely related standard consequences could reduce the independent mathematical contribution.

final_claim: For each fiber of a Néron model of a semi-abelian variety over a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field, |Phi_s[m]|=m^(t_s-t_eta) for all integers m>0 and Phi_s,tors≅(Q/Z)^(t_s-t_eta).
limitations: Algebraically closed generic field is essential; does not cover arbitrary DVRs or classify torsion-free part.
